text:
maria: Heads up — release promotion is blocked. CI job #492 failed in the promote step with an artifact checksum mismatch after cache restore. @deploy-bot is spinning retries.
chris: Logs?
maria: ```\n=== promote-artifact job 492 ===\nRestoring cache from gs://redwood-ci-cache/ci-492\ntar: unexpected EOF in archive\nERROR: artifact checksum mismatch: expected abc123 got def456\nRetries exhausted\n``` 
jen: This sounds like the remote-cache restore we saw last month. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ci-cache-restore
alex: Quick options: pin previous artifact and manual promote, or rerun full pipeline without cache. Pinning needs release lead approval and signed manifest.
sylvia: Change window is open for ~40m. Manual pin + signed manifest is fastest but has security/process steps.
chris: We can try forcing rerun with cache disabled: `CI_RESTORE_CACHE=false ./ci promote --job=492` — but if signing job didn't run in the other pipeline we may still be missing the manifest.
maria: Tried the skip-cache rerun earlier — build passes, but promote fails: signed-manifest job was canceled due to dependency race in parallel workflows.
jen: So two simultaneous faults: corrupt cache restore + signing race. Ugh.
sylvia: Options ranked: 1) manual pin + sign + promote (fastest, needs approval), 2) rerun full pipeline end-to-end (slower, safer), 3) rollback to previous release (impactful). Thoughts?
alex: My preference is manual pin + sign. Chris, can you verify the artifact hash and prepare a signed manifest? If valid I'll ok approval.
chris: On it. I'll verify checksums against storage and re-sign if unchanged. Command I'll run: `sha256sum artifact.tar.gz` then `sign-manifest --artifact-hash sha256:abc999`.
deploy-bot: Action blocked: promotion requires 'release-lead' approval or 'canary' flag. Use `/approve @release-lead` or set `canary:true` in the promote command.
maria: @jen can you approve the manual promote if chris confirms the hash? We need this to go out during change window.
jen: I can approve once Chris posts the verified hash and a short note in the release notes about the manual pin. :thumbsup:
chris: Verified: artifact present in gs://redwood-releases/prod/2026-03-20/abc999, sha256=abc999, signature missing. I'll upload a signed-manifest now and prepare the promote command.
maria: I'll escalate the manual approval in the release doc and ping security for the signed-manifest upload trace.
chris: Running `deploy-bot promote --artifact=abc999 --force --canary=true` (will still require approval but can limit traffic). If anyone objects, say now.
jen: No objection. Approving once you post the signed-manifest sha.
chris: Signed-manifest uploaded: sig=sha256sig:zzz111. Checksums line up. Proceeding with promote.
deploy-bot: Promotion started. Canary flag set, rolling out to 5%.
maria: Moving monitoring to #incidents for the next 20m to watch regressions.
jen: Please add a post-release task to audit cache restore, add a mitigation for tar EOF, and raise an infra ticket.
alex: Noted. Also let's add a CI toggle to decline restoring from older cache blobs if tar errors are seen.
sylvia: Good call. After canary completes we'll decide whether to continue full rollout.
maria: Canary healthy at 5m. No errors so far.
chris: Canary at 20m looks good. Promoting to 100% now.
deploy-bot: Promotion complete.
maria: Thanks everyone — release promoted. I'll update release notes with a 'manual pin due to cache restore corruption' entry and link to the runbook and infra ticket.
jen: Great work. :raised_hands:
maria: closing thread and creating follow-ups in backlog."
